**PREFACE**

The SwasthyaMitra and its conception was a result of observing that nowadays most people find it extremely difficult to remain healthy due to the hectic, technology-intensive world. It was designed to correct the lack of balance of exercise, diet and mental health brought about by the current way of living of sedentary behavior and busy time.

The primary motive of the given project was to fill the existing health apps that typically only track calories or workouts separately. Such a patchwork approach can hardly lead to good health and discourage users. SwasthyaMitra was developed to provide one, intelligent platform that allows people to take charge of their wellness themselves.

One of the driving factors was to provide custom advice on exercise and diet using Artificial Intelligence on a real-time basis. It was part of the study to ensure that the solution is culturally relevant to the solution with the inclusion of the Indian eating habits and festival-sensitive meal planning. The project will fill the gap between scientific nutrition and affordable digital healthcare by introducing new functions that allow inhabitants to monitor their health, maintain mental health, and in case of emergencies, send an emergency SOS alert. Finally, it is a proactive assignment aimed at promoting preventative medicine and developing long-term practices.

**ABSTRACT** 

SwasthyaMitra is an advanced Android-based mobile application designed to support users in managing their overall health and well-being through personalized and intelligent monitoring. The application goes beyond basic health tracking by integrating fitness, nutrition, mental wellness, and lifestyle management into a single platform. It enables users to track important health parameters such as physical activity, sleep patterns, hydration, body metrics, and dietary habits. By using Artificial Intelligence, SwasthyaMitra provides real-time analysis of user data and delivers customized recommendations for diet, exercise.  
The system focuses on culturally relevant and practical health guidance by incorporating Indian dietary habits, festival-aware meal planning, and personalized workout suggestions. It also includes features such as hydration tracking, mood-based wellness support, and women’s health monitoring through the “Period Mode.” The application ensures data privacy and security using Firebase Authentication, Cloud Firestore  , and rule-based access control.

SwasthyaMitra implements scientific approaches such as the Mifflin-St Jeor equation to calculate BMR and TDEE, enabling accurate calorie targeting. Developed using Kotlin, Coroutines, and modern Firebase integration, the project demonstrates contemporary Android development practices. Overall, the application aims to bridge the gap between scientific nutrition, traditional lifestyles, and user-friendly digital healthcare solutions.

**Keywords:** Android Application, Healthcare Tracking, AI Diet and Fitness Planning, Gemini AI, Indian Nutrition.

#  **CHAPTER 1 : INTRODUCTION**

In the modern world, which can be described as a world of busyness, blistering development in scientific technology, the maintenance of a wholesome way of life has become a demanding feat to a significant proportion of the population. An imbalance between physical exercise, diet, and mental health is often the result of higher workloads and widespread sedentary lifestyles and time constraints. In this regard, the current project intends to mitigate such barriers by designing a health and wellness mobile application, SwasthyaMitra, that will purport to empower users to take charge of their health and lifestyle independently.

The main aim of SwasthyaMitra is to provide the users with an insightful, unified, and customized device to monitor and improve their wellbeing, health, and dieting. The app offers a set of bespoke dieting, physical exercise, and overall wellness suggestions with the help of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The general purpose is to streamline the health treatment process by combining multiple functionalities, including activity tracking, nutrition monitoring, and support of mental health into one unified, logical system. Moreover, the application attempts to promulgate preventive healthcare services by inspiring users toward adopting healthy sustenances via custom-made suggestions, careful thought, and heightened consideration.

**1.1 BACKGROUND**

Health, fitness and nutrition management has become a tedious process following the hectic timetable, pervasive lack of consciousness and inadequate availability of personalized advice. Swarming numbers of people are struggling with scattered health monitoring, lack of inspiration, and lack of smart tools to guide them to the realization of their wellness goals.

Modern health and fitness apps have focused mostly on individual areas: caloric counting or workout tracking as such, thus forcing the user to rely on a variety of uncoordinated apps to cater to an uncoordinated area of their health. This fragmentation creates inconsistent aspects and makes it increasingly hard to maintain motivation and lead an energetic life among the users.

Therefore, it is observed that complex, integrative, and digital health solutions are expanding in demand that make real-time, personalised support accessible. The mobile health and wellness apps, therefore, take a central stage in ensuring that health management has become accessible, convenient, and effective.

SwasthyaMitra solves these problems by offering an all-inclusive platform, which gathers fitness monitoring, nutritional monitoring, observation of mental wellness, and safety. The application uses AI to analyze user information, provide personalized options, and help users to keep track of their health, correct habits, and make informed choices. SwasthyaMitra can help users to live healthier balanced lives as it bridges the gap that exists between health awareness and maintaining a healthy lifestyle.

# **1.2 AIM AND OBJECTIVES**

The primary aim of the project SwasthyaMitra : Mobile-Based Health, Fitness, and Nutrition Management App with AI Personalization is to develop an intelligent, user-friendly mobile application that integrates fitness tracking, nutrition management, mental wellness monitoring, and personalized health guidance into a single platform. The app leverages AI to analyze users' activity, diet, sleep, and emotional patterns to provide tailored recommendations, promoting proactive and sustainable health management.

SwasthyaMitra addresses the challenge of maintaining a healthy lifestyle in today’s fast-paced world by eliminating the need for multiple apps and encouraging consistent health monitoring. It focuses on preventive healthcare, offering reminders, progress insights, and educational tips to reduce lifestyle-related health risks.

The app ensures accessibility with a simple interface and uses mobile sensors and Firebase for secure data storage and real-time updates. Gamification features like streaks, badges, and challenges enhance user engagement, while safety features like emergency alerts add reliability. SwasthyaMitra aims to empower individuals to take control of their health through technology, personalization, and motivation.

The main goals of the Swasthya Mitra project are : To offer health and fitness tracking that works in real time.The application lets users track their physical activities in real time by using the device's built-in sensors like accelerometers and GPS. Live step counting, distance measurement, calorie estimation, and tracking exercise sessions help users keep up with their fitness during the day without needing any extra gadgets or wearable devices.

Keep track of daily activities like steps taken, sleep, water drinking, and what you eat. SwasthyaMitra has specific modules to help you keep an eye on your daily health basics. The step counter keeps track of your daily walking and running, showing you a history sorted by date. The sleep tracker lets users record how long they sleep and look at their sleep patterns over time.The smart diet and nutrition module lets users log their meals, scan food barcodes to get nutrition details, and keep a detailed food diary. Together, these features give users a full view of their daily health habits.

The idea is to give health and wellness advice that fits each person, using artificial intelligence. The application uses an AI-powered coaching system that looks at the user’s tracked data—like activity levels, eating habits, mood logs, and health goals—to create personalized suggestions and practical advice.These recommendations change over time as the user's habits and health data change, making sure the advice stays useful, realistic, and fits the person's current needs and goals.

The aim is to boost user engagement and motivation by adding gamification features like rewards, streaks, and challenges. The app knows that keeping up new habits takes steady motivation, so it includes a full gamification setup.Users get experience points and achievement badges when they complete health tasks. They keep daily streaks going to stay motivated and can join organized wellness challenges.These parts create a feeling of achievement and friendly competition that helps people stay involved with their health goals for a long time.

It provides a simple “Period Mode” option, which female users can activate during their menstrual cycle. Based on this mode, the app suggests suitable diet and exercise recommendations to help manage discomfort and maintain health. This feature ensures that the application goes beyond basic fitness tracking and addresses the specific needs of women.

The aim is to keep users safe by providing emergency alerts and support options.The application has a safety module that includes an SOS emergency alert feature.If someone feels unsafe or has a health emergency, the app can quickly send alert messages with their current location to emergency contacts they set up beforehand.This feature gives an important boost to personal safety, making the app helpful for more than just regular health tracking.

The goal is to create health reports, analytics, and insights that help with making better decisions.SwasthyaMitra gives users clear dashboards and progress reports that show their health data over time.By using graphs that show step counts, weight changes, sleep habits, exercise routines, and food logs, users can see clear patterns, keep track of their progress, and make smarter choices about their health and lifestyle based on real data, not just guesses.

The goal is to create an interface that’s easy to use, straightforward, and feels natural for anyone.One main goal of the project is to make sure the application is simple and easy to use for people of all ages and different levels of tech skill.The user interface follows Material Design principles, with simple layouts, matching colour schemes, easy navigation, and screens arranged logically. This way, users can reach any feature quickly, making it easier to learn and improving how they experience the app.

The aim is to spread the word about taking care of your health early and building good habits.SwasthyaMitra doesn’t just track and monitor; it also wants to teach users why preventive health practices matter.The app offers health tips based on your context, mood-focused wellness suggestions, nutrition advice, and coaching insights created by AI. It helps users build healthier habits ahead of time instead of waiting for problems to come up.This preventive approach fits with the bigger aim of encouraging a health-conscious mindset, especially among younger users.

**1.4.2. Overall Description**

**Product Perspective**  
SwasthyaMitra is a mobile application designed to act as a personal health companion. It integrates various health and wellness features, such as fitness tracking, nutrition management, and mental wellness monitoring, into a single platform. The app uses AI to provide personalized recommendations and insights based on user data, promoting a healthier lifestyle.

**Product Functions**

* Track daily steps, activity, sleep, hydration, and mood.  
* Provide personalized diet and exercise recommendations using AI.  
* Enable users to log food, exercise.   
* Offer gamification features like streaks, badges, and rewards.  
* Provide safety features like emergency SOS alerts.  
* Generate health reports and analytics for user progress tracking.  
* Send notifications and reminders for health-related tasks

**User Classes and Characteristics**

* General Users: Individuals looking to improve their health and wellness.  
* Fitness Enthusiasts: Users with specific fitness goals like weight loss or muscle gain.  
* Women: Users who require additional features like menstrual health tracking.  
* Students/Young Adults: Users who need motivation and reminders for consistent health tracking.

**Operating Environment**

* Platform: Android (minimum version 8.0 or higher).  
* Hardware: Android smartphones with GPS, accelerometer, and internet connectivity.  
* Backend: Firebase for authentication, database, and AI integration.

**Design and Implementation Constraints**

* The app must comply with Android design guidelines.  
* Limited to Android devices with specific hardware capabilities (e.g., GPS, accelerometer).  
* Data security and privacy must adhere to GDPR and other relevant regulations.

**Assumptions and Dependencies**

* Users will have access to an Android device with an active internet connection.  
* Firebase services will be available and functional.  
* Users will provide accurate personal and health data for better recommendations.

* Description: Sends reminders for health-related tasks.  
* Inputs: User preferences and schedules.  
* Outputs: Timely notifications and reminders.  
* Processing: Schedule and send notifications.  
* Conditions: Requires user input and internet access.

# **CHAPTER 2 : LITERATURE REVIEW**

**2.1 Survey of Fitness and Nutrition Application**

This literature survey review has eight android mobile apps that have advanced nutrition and fitness management features without requiring wearable devices. This survey is conducted by choosing the apps according to their popularity, android compatibility, feature relevance, like MyFitnessPal, Cronometer, FitOn, Home Workout, Hevy, PUSH, Lose It, and Healthify. This review looks at how all the apps handle all the features from basic habit tracking to athletic training, it focuses on how accurate and easy to use all these apps are.

**2.1.1 Overview**  
   
**2.1.1 MyFitnessPal**  
Leading the nutrition-tracking market, MyFitnessPal provides an enormous global customer base with a platform to accurately record macronutrients and calories consumed to be compared with daily energy burnt. Its major strength is an extensive food database, supplemented by crowdsourced input including infrequent or brand-specific ones.  
The app can be easily connected to wearables like Garmin and Apple Health, and the vibrant social environment has a significant impact on behavioural compliance. However, the basis of the system on a user-created information presents observable errors, especially in macronutrient granularity. There are also critical functions, such as precise timestamping and barcode scanning, which are restricted by a subscription, which limits the functionality of the free version.

**2.1.2 Cronometer**  
Cronometer caters more to health experts and bio-hackers by going in advance with sophisticated micro-nutrient tracking, as opposed to naive calorie debriefing. It ensures the highest level of data integrity by obtaining only officially confirmed data sources e.g. by the USDA avoiding the traps found in crowdsourced inputs. It tracks more than eighty-two individual micronutrients, thereby fitting well with the clinical dietary protocols, such as vegan or ketogenic diets, and allows the user to compare dietary use to physiological parameters, such as blood pressure and glucose.  
On the other hand, this incredibly analytic and utilitarian interface creates an uphill learning curve among those who are not experts, and purposely lacks significant social interaction, instead focusing on individual data analysis more than group promotion.

**2.1.3 Healthify**  
Healthify or formerly known as HealthifyMe is specifically a product built to suit the Indian market and is a combination of artificial intelligence and human coaching to optimize metabolic wellness. Its carefully maintained database of the complex caloric fineries of various regional Indian dishes is incredibly precise. Users can get access to Ria, a generative Al assistant which provides contextually sensitive dietary advice in real-time, with an augmenting visual "Snap" assistant that lets one scan a whole meal in one scan. Although the innovations are apparent, the platform is heavily feature bloated, as it enriches the application with diagnostics, e-commerce features, and constant upsells on premium services, thus overloading the basic food-tracking layout and losing the user focus on the main workflow, making it a little discontinuous.

**2.1.4 FitOn**  
As a high-end online studio, FitOn adopts a content-based approach, which implies providing high-quality workout streams led by celebrities. The platform has done a good job of breaking the barrier to entry since this professional-level content is available at no cost or at a fixed cost in many cases. The live-class environment and enhanced production quality are used to contribute greatly towards the motivation of the user.  
However, in comparison with specialized diet-tracking programs, its diet planning software is rather unsophisticated. Moreover, the high-intensity nature of the use of the app, which requires constant and high-speed video streaming, makes it virtually impossible to use by people who live in areas where the internet is not as reliable or as fast as it should be.

**2.1.5 Home Workout**   
This specific app is also accessible bodyweight conditioning, tailored to people who do not have access to the traditional gym equipment. It is best applicable at a global scale since it does not require an internet connection or extra equipment, making it also specifically suitable in environments that are limited in resources. Its theistically spartan, straight panel interface alleviates possible decision paralysis amongst beginners. On the other hand, the exercise program is fixed, thus it does not take into account factors of fatigue or the need of progressive overload of an individual. Moreover, the lack of in-built nutritional features requires users to track food available through different apps.

**2.1.6 Lose It\!**  
Lose It\! reshapes the traditional way of calculating a calorie content into a highly gamified process of weight management by focusing on the purposeful use of visual information as the key element of the entry. By designing the application with imitating challenges and friendliness interface, the clinical atmosphere that comes with dieting is eliminated thus enhancing better user retention in the long-term. Further, it was the first company to introduce, through its Snap It Photo-recognition, visual logging. Still, the free one has a strong macronutrient tunnel vision; the users get guided much more in plain caloric counts with neglecting more global and holistic objectives like micronutrients density or daily fiber consumption.

**2.1.7 Hevy**  
Hevy is an easy-to-use and very popular digital gym journal, designed mainly with the purpose of the weightlifter who wants to meticulously document sets, repetitions, and loads, with the highest levels of efficiency. Its most notable characteristic is an aesthetically immaculate interface that will lessen the time one will effectively require consulting his/her mobile device amidst exercises. Secondly, Hevy includes a rich social network where users can follow each other, share workouts using routines and compete in leaderboards, which can be taken as a strong motivational anchor. Still, it is a plain tracker: there is no Al-based coaching or long-term periodization planning. Instead, assuming that somebody using it is already skilled in creating their own programs. Although a free version can be used, it only allows users four custom routine templates and only restricts historical progress graphs to three months.

**2.1.8 PUSH App**  
Focusing on clients who were dedicated to hypertrophy specifically, PUSH is an Al-based fitness app, which builds and modifies exercise routines through algorithms that are directly based on scientific literature reviewed by peers. It has the advantage of an auto-adaptive, ultra-polished interface, which automatically adjusts the volume, the frequency, and the rep range to the daily levels of fatigue, sleep, and experience, this is in the elimination of the guesswork that is involved in the progressive overload. Most of its science-based automation is remarkable, but the application cannot be used in other disciplines of fitness besides muscle building and does not aid cardio or mobility.

Moreover, it has a high price which customers must pay annually, and customers have occasionally complained of quaint Al recommendations, like unrealistic weight loss, as well as a bulky absence of being Apple Watch compatible, which hinders smooth gym tracking.

**2.2 TECHNOLOGY FRAMEWORKS**

By analyzing the health related applications like MyFitnessPal, Healthyfy,Hevy, PUSH, Lose It and FitOn, we found that these applications have diverse user goals ranging from nutrition and dietary management to body training by influencing refined mobile applications  . Some of these applications like MyFitnessPal, Lose It\! Cronometer has many food databases with up to ten million entries , also it has barcode scanning and image recognition for well organized caloric and micro nutrient logging. Applications such as FitOn and Home Workout rely on strong content delivery systems that provide online exercise video classes and offline animated exercise routines. Platforms such as Hevy and PUSH  use predictive analytics and evidence-based progressive logic to optimise strength training features for advanced users. Furthersome , artificial intelligence is being  used more and more by synchronized hybrid applications such as MadMuscles to create customised, integrated meal and exercise plans.

**3.5 ALGORITHMS**  
An algorithm is a well-defined, step-by-step procedure that describes the logic behind how a particular task or computation is performed within a system. In software development, algorithms form the backbone of decision-making, data processing, and automation. In the context of SwasthyaMitra, algorithms are used extensively to calculate health metrics, generate personalised food and exercise recommendations, track daily activities, and adapt suggestions based on user behaviour over time. This section presents the key algorithms used in the system in a clear, numbered format and explains the logic behind each one.

**3.5.1 Algorithm 1: BMI and BMR Calculation**  
Step 1: Accept height (in cm), weight (in kg), age (in years), and gender from the user profile.  
Step 2: Convert height from centimetres to metres by dividing by 100\.  
Step 3: Calculate BMI using the formula: BMI \= weight / (height in metres)².  
Step 4: Classify the BMI result as Underweight (below 18.5), Normal (18.5 to 24.9), Overweight (25.0 to 29.9), or Obese (30.0 and above).  
Step 5: Calculate BMR using the Mifflin-St Jeor equation: Base BMR \= (10 × weight) \+ (6.25 × height in cm) − (5 × age).  
Step 6: If the user is male, add 5 to the base BMR. If the user is female, subtract 161 from the base BMR.  
Step 7: Store the BMI and BMR values for use in subsequent algorithms.  
The Mifflin-St Jeor equation is considered one of the most accurate methods for estimating resting metabolic rate in modern populations. These values are recalculated whenever the user updates their weight or profile information, ensuring that downstream recommendations remain accurate.

**3.5.2 Algorithm 2: Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) and Target Calorie Calculation**  
Step 1: Retrieve the BMR value calculated in Algorithm 1\.  
Step 2: Retrieve the user's activity level from their lifestyle data. The possible levels are Sedentary, Lightly Active, Moderately Active, and Very Active.  
Step 3: Assign an activity multiplier: Sedentary \= 1.2, Lightly Active \= 1.375, Moderately Active \= 1.55, Very Active \= 1.725.  
Step 4: Calculate TDEE by multiplying BMR by the activity multiplier: TDEE \= BMR × Activity Factor.  
Step 5: Retrieve the user's fitness goal. The possible goals are Weight Loss, Muscle Gain, and Stay Healthy.  
Step 6: If the goal is Weight Loss, subtract 500 calories from the TDEE.  
Step 7: If the goal is Muscle Gain, add 300 calories to the TDEE.  
Step 8: If the goal is Stay Healthy, use the TDEE value as the target calories.  
Step 9: Store the target calorie value for use in the diet planning algorithms.  
This algorithm is based on the scientific principle that one kilogram of body fat is equivalent to approximately 7,700 calories.

**3.5.3 Algorithm 3: Macronutrient Distribution**  
Step 1: Retrieve the target calorie value from Algorithm 2\.  
Step 2: Retrieve the user's fitness goal.  
Step 3: If the goal is Weight Loss, set the ratios to 30% protein, 40% carbohydrates, and         
 30% fat.   
Step 4: If the goal is Muscle Gain, set the ratios to 25% protein, 50% carbohydrates, and 25% fat.  
Step 5: If the goal is Stay Healthy, set the ratios to 20% protein, 50% carbohydrates, and 30% fat.  
Step 6: Calculate grams of each macronutrient using the conversion factors.  
Step 7: Protein (grams) \= (target calories × protein ratio) / 4\.  
Step 8: Carbohydrates (grams) \= (target calories × carbohydrate ratio) / 4\.  
Step 9: Fat (grams) \= (target calories × fat ratio) / 9\.  
Step 10: Return the macronutrient targets as part of the daily nutrition goal.

**3.5.4 Algorithm 4: AI-Powered Personalised Diet Plan Generation**  
Step 1: Retrieve the user's profile data including age, gender, weight, height, dietary preference.  
Step 2: Retrieve the user's fitness goal and activity level.  
Step 3: Calculate BMR, TDEE, and target calories using Algorithms 1 and 2\.  
Step 4: Fetch the user's food logs from the past seven days.  
Step 5: Extract distinct food items consumed recently.  
Step 6: Fetch the user's list of disliked foods.  
Step 7: Fetch the user's recent exercise logs from the past three days.  
Step 8: If high-intensity workouts are detected, set an intensity flag.  
Step 9: Fetch the user's weight logs from the past fourteen days.  
Step 10: Detect weight plateau if the difference is less than 0.2 kg.  
Step 11: Check the current date against Indian festivals.  
Step 12: Determine the current season.  
Step 13: Check if period mode is enabled.  
Step 14: Build a comprehensive prompt and send it to Gemini 2.0 Flash.  
Step 15: Parse the AI response into a MealPlan object.  
Step 16: Validate the plan for dietary compliance.  
Step 17: Save the validated plan to Firestore.  
Step 18: If the AI fails, return a fallback meal plan.  
**3.5.5 Algorithm 5: AI-Powered Exercise Recommendation**  
Step 1: Retrieve the user's age, gender, weight, and fitness goal.  
Step 2: Load exercise datasets from application assets.  
Step 3: Check if period mode is enabled.  
Step 4: Apply filtering based on period safety.  
Step 5: Filter exercises with visual demonstrations.  
Step 6: Retrieve the user's current mood.  
Step 7: Retrieve today's food logs and calories.  
Step 8: Determine the time of day.  
Step 9: Construct and send the prompt to Gemini 2.0 Flash.  
Step 10: Parse the AI response into structured exercises.  
Step 11: Match exercises with GIFs or images.  
Step 12: Display the workout session.

**3.5.6 Algorithm 6: Step Counting with GPS Cross-Validation**  
Step 1: Register listeners for step detector and accelerometer sensors.  
Step 2: Check timing between consecutive steps.  
Step 3: Accumulate raw steps in a rolling thirty-second window.  
Step 4: Compare step distance with GPS distance.  
Step 5: Calibrate stride length dynamically.  
Step 6: Perform cadence validation using speed.  
Step 7: Apply activity-aware filtering.  
Step 8: Detect anomalies and discard invalid data.  
Step 9: Output validated steps and update UI.

**3.5.7 Algorithm 7: Personalised Water Intake Goal Calculation**  
Step 1: Retrieve the user's weight.  
Step 2: Calculate the base water goal: Weight × 33\.  
Step 3: Retrieve activity level.  
Step 4: Adjust water intake based on activity.  
Step 5: Apply lower and upper bounds.  
Step 6: Store the calculated goal.  
Step 7: Display the recommended intake range.

**3.5.8 Algorithm 8: AI Coach Behaviour-Aware Messaging**  
Step 1: Retrieve the user's name, goal, and calorie target.  
Step 2: Retrieve today's food logs and nutrients.  
Step 3: Retrieve water intake and goal.  
Step 4: Retrieve step count and calories burned.  
Step 5: Check exercise completion.  
Step 6: Calculate Activity Score.  
Step 7: Perform behaviour analysis.  
Step 8: Send the structured prompt to Gemini 2.0 Flash.  
Step 9: Generate personalised coaching messages.  
Step 10: If AI fails, return a fallback message.

**3.5.9 Algorithm 9: Gamification — Streak, Shield, and XP Management**  
Step 1: Calculate days since last active date.  
Step 2: Update streak count.  
Step 3: Use shields if days are missed.  
Step 4: Award bonus shields.  
Step 5: Check step-based shield rewards.  
Step 6: Add XP for health actions.  
Step 7: Check level-up thresholds.  
Step 8: Unlock badges.  
Step 9: Persist gamification data.

**3.5.10 Algorithm 10: Weight Projection**  
Step 1: Calculate base daily calorie burn.  
Step 2: Retrieve daily calories consumed.  
Step 3: Retrieve exercise calories.  
Step 4: Calculate daily calorie balance.  
Step 5: Convert calorie balance to weight change.  
Step 6: Update projected weight.  
Step 7: Synchronise with actual logs.  
Step 8: Plot weight trend.

**3.5.11 Algorithm 11: Mood-Based Recommendation**  
    Step 1: Accept mood and intensity.  
    Step 2: Perform local mood analysis.  
    Step 3: Build and send a prompt to Gemini 2.0 Flash.  
    Step 4: Receive food, exercise, and wellness suggestions.  
    Step 5: Parse and display recommendations.

**3.5.12 How the Algorithms Support Adaptive Personalisation**  
The algorithms described in this section do not operate in isolation. They form an interconnected system where the output of one algorithm feeds into the input of another, creating a continuously adaptive personalisation loop. The BMI and BMR values from Algorithm 1 flow into the TDEE calculation of Algorithm 2, which in turn determines the calorie targets used by the diet plan generator in Algorithm 4\. The food logs recorded through the daily tracking system become exclusion inputs for the next day's diet plan, ensuring that the AI never recommends the same food repeatedly. The exercise data influences the diet plan by triggering post-workout meal suggestions when high-intensity sessions are detected. The gamification algorithm rewards users for consistent tracking behaviour, which in turn produces more data for the AI algorithms to generate better recommendations. The AI Coach in Algorithm 8 synthesises real-time data from steps, meals, water, and exercise to deliver a contextually relevant message at every interaction. As the user continues to use the application over days and weeks, the system accumulates more behavioural data, and the recommendations become increasingly tailored to the individual's habits, preferences, and health patterns. This feedback-driven design is what makes SwasthyaMitra not just a health tracker but a truly personalised health companion.

**CHAPTER 4 : ANALYSIS, RESULTS AND DISCUSSION**

**4.1 MODULE-WISE ANALYSIS**

This section presents a brief analysis of each major module in the Swasthya Mitra application, covering its purpose, key features, how users interact with it, and the benefits it provides.

**4.1.1 Authentication and Onboarding Module**  
This module manages user registration, login, session persistence, and a three-step onboarding process. Users sign up with email, password, name, phone number, and date of birth. After login, the system checks whether the user has completed their physical profile, selected a fitness goal, and provided lifestyle preferences. The user is directed to the appropriate onboarding screen for any missing step. A persistent login check using SharedPreferences allows returning users to skip the login screen entirely.

This module ensures that complete health data is available before any recommendation feature is used. It also provides forgot-password functionality through Firebase Authentication’s email reset.

**4.1.2 Homepage and Dashboard Module**  
The homepage is the central hub that displays a real-time summary of the user's daily health status. It shows an AI-generated coaching message, calorie balance, macronutrient totals, step count, water intake progress, workout count, and weight goal progress.

Navigation cards provide quick access to all feature modules. A Period Mode chip, visible only for female users, adjusts all AI recommendations when activated. The homepage also initializes background notification workers for water and meal reminders.  
This module gives users a single-screen overview of their entire health day.

**4.1.3 Food Logging Module**  
Users can log meals through three methods:

* Searching an offline Indian food database.  
* Manual entry with auto-suggested meal type.  
* Barcode scanning using CameraX and ML Kit.  
* 

All entries are stored in Firestore with calorie, protein, carbohydrate, fat, meal type, and timestamp fields. A daily summary displays total intake across nutrients.

This module provides flexibility for different user scenarios such as quick logging, detailed input, and packaged food scanning.

**4.1.4 AI Smart Diet Plan Module**  
This module generates a complete daily meal plan personalized to the user’s metabolic calculations (BMR and TDEE), fitness goal, dietary preference, recent eating history, exercise intensity, weight plateau detection, current season, festival awareness, and menstrual health status.

The Gemini 2.0 Flash AI model generates breakfast, lunch, snacks, dinner, and post-workout meals. Each suggestion includes calories, protein, a reason, and a tip.  
Dietary compliance is validated after generation, and meals can be regenerated or skipped. A fallback plan is provided when the AI is unavailable. This module delivers adaptive nutrition advice that changes daily.

**4.1.5 Exercise and Workout Module**  
The Workout Dashboard provides AI-powered exercise recommendations. The system loads exercises from four local datasets containing more than 800 exercises with GIF demonstrations.

Exercises are filtered based on the user’s profile, mood, fitness goal, and period mode. Gemini AI generates structured sessions including warm-up, main workout, and cool-down with instructions and tips.  
This module combines databases with AI to provide personalized and visually guided workouts.

**4.1.6 Step Counting Module**  
The step counter uses a five-layer GPS cross-validation system:

* GPS distance validation  
* Dynamic stride calibration  
* Speed-based cadence checking  
* Activity recognition filtering  
* Anomaly detection


Steps are counted only during user-initiated sessions, reducing false counts.  
This module ensures significantly higher accuracy than basic pedometer systems.

**4.1.7 Sleep Tracking Module**  
Users log sleep through quick one-tap buttons or detailed input. A two-stage duplicate check prevents multiple entries per day.  
This module ensures consistent sleep tracking with minimal user effort.

**4.1.8 Hydration Tracking Module**  
The daily water goal is calculated based on body weight and activity. Progress is displayed visually.  
Reminders use both WorkManager and AlarmManager to ensure reliability.  
This module helps users maintain proper hydration habits.

**4.1.9 Mood Tracking and Recommendation Module**  
Users select moods such as Happy, Calm, Tired, Sad, or Stressed. A rule-based system provides immediate suggestions, while Gemini AI generates personalized recommendations.  
Mood history is visualized through charts.  
This module connects emotional well-being with actionable health advice.

**4.1.10 Gamification Module**  
This module includes:

* Daily streaks  
* Experience points  
* Levels  
* Badges  
* Shield protection

These features encourage consistent engagement and habit formation.

**4.1.11 Safety Core Module**  
This module provides:

* SOS emergency alerts  
* Emergency contact management  
* Ghost Mode tracking  
* Live GPS sharing

It enhances user safety beyond health tracking.

**4.1.12 Progress Dashboard and Insights Module**  
This module shows health trends over 7, 15, and 30 days. It includes achievement stages and a Workout Balance Score.  
Insights and micro-goals are generated based on weekly behaviour.

**4.1.13 Smart Pantry Module**  
Users photograph kitchen ingredients, and Gemini AI generates recipes with nutritional values.  
This module helps reduce food waste and promotes healthy cooking.

**4.1.14 Profile and Settings Module**  
Users can edit personal data, view BMI, BMR, and TDEE, and manage notifications.  
This module ensures complete user control.

**4.3 RESULTS**

This section presents key observations from the developed system.

**4.3.1 Accuracy of Health Calculations**  
BMI, BMR, and TDEE calculations use the Mifflin-St Jeor equation and WHO standards. The system shows high accuracy with approximately ±10% error.  
The step counter’s validation system reduces false counts.  
Water goals align with global health recommendations.

**4.3.2 Efficiency of AI Recommendations**  
Gemini AI provides fast responses within 3–8 seconds.  
Retry and fallback mechanisms ensure continuous guidance even during network issues.  
Diet diversity is maintained through food exclusion logic.

**4.3.3 User Engagement through Gamification**  
The reward system motivates daily usage. Shield protection reduces discouragement from missed days.  
Achievement stages guide users toward consistency.  
**4.3.4 Effectiveness of Personalisation**  
Personalization occurs at multiple levels:

* Metabolic  
* Preference  
* Contextual  
* Behavioural

This makes the system more adaptive and user-centric.

**4.4 DISCUSSION**

**4.4.1 Comparison with Existing Applications**  
Compared to popular apps such as MyFitnessPal, HealthifyMe, Google Fit, and Samsung Health, Swasthya Mitra offers deeper AI personalization, Indian food focus, safety features, and context-aware recommendations.

**4.4.2 Advantages of Swasthya Mitra**  
The major strengths include:

* Deep AI personalization  
* Indian-focused nutrition  
* Accurate step tracking  
* Safety features  
* Offline food logging  
* Advanced gamification

**4.4.3 Limitations**  
Some limitations include:

* Dependence on internet for AI  
* Manual food logging  
* Battery usage due to GPS  
* Android-only availability  
* Occasional AI inaccuracies

**4.4.4 Challenges Faced During Development**  
Key challenges included:

* Managing multiple Firebase databases  
* Ensuring dietary compliance  
* Improving step accuracy  
* Handling AI delays and failures


**4.4.5 Scope for Future Improvements**  
Future enhancements include:

* Food image recognition  
* Wearable integration  
* Social and community features  
* Multilingual support  
* iOS version  
* Predictive health analytics  
  




**CHAPTER 5 : CONCLUSION, LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE WORK**

**5.1 CONCLUSION**

In modern times, the spread of lifestyle related health issues highlights the need of a convenient, smart, personally tailored health application. SwasthyaMitra is a well considered and highly intelligent creation designed to meet this urgency and it operates not as an application, but as a digital companion that will help a user move towards comprehensive wellbeing. The effective combination of current technology in mobile devices and nutrition science makes the effort to provide an all embracive, empirically based solution that enables people to take active responsibility in the management of their health by making informed choices and attentively observing the state of their bodies.

SwasthayaMitra can reduce the inbuilt complexities of health management towards a functional perspective. The application does not flood users with raw information, but it will provide actionable insights instead. Other modules like the Diet Recommendation System and Meal Planning facilitate the conversion of abstract nutritional goals into real life, essential habits. The package of tracking tools Food Logging to the approved Progress Monitoring provides long-term responsibility and motivation. In addition, the intuitive user interface created with an uncompromising adherence to the principle of accessibility enables users with varying technical expertise levels to find their way to such components of the application as Profile Management and Goal Setting with ease. Such user experience is a reflection of the philosophic principle of the project: technology must add nothing new to any impediments to health.

On technical fronts, SwasthyaMitra can be a testimony on how powerful the modern Android production can be. Written in Kotlin, the application leverages the power of a modern, statically-typed and safety-guaranteeing programming language with code safety and efficiency ensuring computation. The architectural blueprint follows industry-standard patterns, and there is a supposed implementation of MVVM (ModelViewViewModel) principles that are supported with the Android Jetpack components, ViewModel and LiveData, which separate the business logic and user interface, resulting in a stable system and responsive platform.

One of the technical achievements that are salient in this project is the combination of machine learning and advanced hardware usage. The work of the Barcode Scanner that is a project of the ML Kit in Google allows retrieving nutritional information instantly, which in turn easily connects the real world with the virtual one. In a related complementary manner, CameraX also offers similar, high-quality camera experience on the wide range of Android gadgets when performing features like food capture. The back-end system, which is based on Firebase, provides a server-less economy that handles authentication in a secure manner and coordinates real-time data operations using Cloud Firestore. As a result, user information is automatically updated in real-time intersession and is protected by security measures on an industry level. The fact that the application has incorporated Retrofit to operate in the network to manipulate document formats like Excel is another testimony to this nature of scalability and ability of complex data reporting.

To conclude, SwasthyaMitra is not just a set of code files glued together, it is a complete ecosystem created to improve the quality of life. With the skillful combination of user-friendly design and powerful supporting technologies, namely, ML Kit and Firebase, and Jetpack libraries, the project achieves its most important goal of making health management approachable and exciting. As digital health foretells a progression of constant transformation, SwasthyaMitra lays a solid groundwork of future improvements, including Al-based predictive health analytics, thus substantiating the fact that a reasonable combination of a benevolent will and hard code can truly make a society healthier

**5.2 LIMITATIONS**

Even the most advanced software is surrounded by a set of constraints. SwasthyaMitra being a powerful health and lifestyle app is not an exception to this rule. Getting acquainted with these constraints is not only a way of maintaining realistic projection but also an eye-opener on improving oneself in the future.

**5.2.1 Profane and Unexclusivity of Platform and Device.**  
SwasthyaMitra can be used only on Android. This leaves people who own an iphone and tablets as well as those who are interested in using the application through a web browser with no access to its capabilities. 

There is also hardware capability that is needed in the application to be used optimally. Alterations like Barcode Scanning and Food Photo Capture are examples of functions that depend on the quality of cameras of a device. In case of the sub-optimal camera or non-functional camera, such capabilities will become useless. Furthermore, a version of the Android OS may also develop compatibility issues, namely operating an outdated version. SwasthyaMitra is not designed to serve older hardware.

**5.2.2 Addiction to Internet Connectivity.**  
SwasthyaMitra is significantly dependent on cloud computing, and user authentication, data storage and synchronization between devices are performed on Firebase. Although this architecture guarantees that the user information is updated on various platforms, it requires constant access to the internet. Without connectivity, the users will not be able to log in, to write daily objectives, and map meal plans. 

The latency of real-time services, including calorie tracking and profile synchronisation, will also be affected in environments where the internet is not available at all times. Without a connection, it is not possible to have real-time data exchange, which leads to non-moving data.

**5.2.3 Medical Disclaimers and Scope.**  
It is the desire of SwasthyaMitra to help in optimising lifestyle choices and not to replace professional medical advice. The mentoring and monitoring would hence be considered as informative but not final. 

Persons with underlying health issues like diabetes or hypertension should consult his or her health provider before taking the diet or physical exercise plans embodied by the application. In addition, the meal plans and nutritional advice have a general applicability occurring without taking into consideration specialized medical diets unless explicitly specified to be so. Currently, the application does not recommend physiological parameters in real-time

**5.2.4 Database and Limitation Recognition.**  
In the database case, it involves limitations related to methods used to identify the database's data.human Database and Recognition Limitations In the database case, it is the limits of identification pitchfalls of the data in the database.

The Barcode Scanner and food logging capabilities are dependent on the depth of the supporting database. Even though the application can be effective with the standard packaged foods, the regional cuisine, homemade recipes, or local food might not be recognised, providing empty results. This restriction is of great challenge to users who majorly consume non-packaged foods in their diets.

Image-processing algorithms are employed by the Food Photo Capture component to identify everything in a plate, although it also falsely recognizes stuff and is especially inaccurate when it comes to composite dishes, odd lighting conditions, or poor camera resolution. In this case, the inferred data would need to be corrected by the user.

**5.3 FUTURE WORK** 

Since SwasthyaMitra is subject to change into an all-inclusive health ecosystem, rather than operating within the current blueprint, there are various strategic paths to improvement. The map of the further direction focuses on the increased technological integration, the heightened input of users and the narrowing of the gap between lifestyle tracking and clinical health management. The ensuing defines the key pillars upon which this upcoming development will be directed.

**5.3.1 The Intelligence of the Al showing nutrition.**  
The latest version of nutrient tracking requires fixed repositories and the inputs made by users manually. The next step will include Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) that will fundamentally change the relationship between the users and their dietary information fundamentally.

**5.3.2 Visual Food Recognition:**  
 With the help of computer-vision models that are run on, The "Food Photo Capture" feature will become less primitive in storing images and become truly live. The application will recognize dishes, estimate the size of portions through depth sensing and automatically record the caloric and macronutrient content, which will significantly decrease the apathy that people generally experience towards manual logging which is the number one reason people are not willing to continue using diet apps.

Clever Replacements: The Al will suggest healthier options to logged foods dynamically (i.e. propose a specific fruit instead of a processed snack) depending on the specific objective of the user's weight loss or building muscle.

**5.3.3 Professional Interface Telehealth and Professional Interface.**  
In order to reduce the distance between lifestyle wellness and clinical medicine, a prototype interface is anticipated to be called Pro-Connect.Specifically, our meal logging service is available in multiple formats

**5.3.4 Dietitian Dashboard**  
 Users can provide verified physicians/nutritionists with temporary, non-editing access to their information. This dashboard will provide visualization of trends in weight, consumption, and exercise within weeks or months and allow professionals to implement data-supported recommendations instead of basing recommendations on the patient's memory.

Report Generation: A single-click generation of PDF health reports that can be easily distributed during medical exams will illuminate glucose (when logged by hand), weight change, and nutrition compliance hence transforming the application into a personal tracker to an authentic clinical tool.

**5.3.5 MitraPlay gamification feature**  
This is a gamification módulo integrated into this project, which has a retention-focused direction and shapes the habit formation of users. It proposes the adoption of a dynamic system of "Missiones" a day, whose model of punctuation will administer and grant points to the users, which have a direct effect on their levels of progression and progress chain of consecutive activity. 

The integrity of the data will be ensured through a level verification methodology with the following components: manual registration on the basis of trust, automatic tracking on sensors, GPS and pedometers, as well as system validation with time constraints, transforming the tracks of the salud into a great attraction experience.

**5.3.6 Offline-First Model and Data privacy.**  
The technical architecture will be shifted so that it becomes Inclusive and reliable so as to enable Offline-First model would be utilized where local databases (e.g., Room) will be used in the technical architecture and later synchronize with Firebase once connection has been restored. This will ensure that remote users are not affected, as they can still make their meal logs and view plans despite the distance.

The new models of AI proposed to encompass food recognition and recommendations in the future will be designed to be privacy-friendly, given the sensitivity of the data it concerns. This ensures personal images and detailed health records are calculated on-site and only anonymized and general insights are sent to the cloud to be continuously improved and, therefore, meet the highest standards of data privacy.
